findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, cross-principal denial
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check builds permDenialKey from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent only, without IdentityType. Different identity types can share the same UID string, e.g. anonymous:0 yields UID 0 and render:0 also yields UID 0, and user vs service-account can share UID strings. A denial cached for one principal will therefore cause Check for a different principal with the same UID/action/resource to return Allowed:false without consulting the DB, incorrectly denying e.g. renderer reads that should always be allowed.

findings.title: Denial cache short-circuit reintroduces stale deny after grant
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check returns Allowed:false immediately on permDenialCache hit without requerying the DB, and caches every DB-computed denial for shortCacheTTL (30s). If permissions are granted after a denial was cached, the user continues to be denied until TTL expiry. This reintroduces the same staleness window the PR claims to fix, just moved from permCache to permDenialCache.

findings.title: List serves stale cached permissions with no DB fallback
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go List uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and if it hits returns that stale map directly to listPermission, only querying the DB on cache miss. Unlike Check which falls back to the DB when cached perms deny, List has no revalidation. A dashboard/folder created after the permCache entry was populated will be missing from List Items/Folders for up to 30s, so the stated goal of fetching newly created dashboards/folders is not fixed for list operations.

findings.title: False deny from stale folder tree is cached in denial cache
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check refreshes permissions from the DB on cached deny but reuses the same cached folderTree inside checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions for both the cached and fresh evaluation. If folderCache is stale, the fresh evaluation can still return false, and that false is then stored in permDenialCache. The result stacks TTLs: a stale tree causes a denial entry that continues to deny even after the folder cache refreshes, extending the deny window beyond either TTL alone.

findings.title: Denial-cache test stores deny instead of allow
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go TestService_CacheCheck Should deny on explicit cache deny entry sets permCache to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} with a comment saying it allows access to prove the denial cache is checked first. Since the value is false, checkPermission would deny even without the denial cache, so the test passes whether or not the denial short-circuit works. It should store true to prove precedence, leaving the denial path effectively untested.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous with underscore separator
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name and parent with _ separators. UIDs, dashboard names and folder UIDs can contain _, so different tuples can produce the same key (e.g. name b_c parent d vs name b parent c_d). A collision causes one resource's denial to incorrectly deny a different resource.
